## Blood of the Moon

_CD1: The "Study in Forces" Series_

**DJ Jaya Prime**

\[[Stream on Mixcloud](https://www.mixcloud.com/JayaPrime/blood-of-the-moon/)\]

There are over a dozen different mutations of this mix floating around out there -- it's been chopped, screwed, and re-mixed since 2k2. The latest cut is purpose-built for the MP3 era, breaking down the mammoth set into easily digestible three-to-four-song subsets. They hit easier than a massive hour-long file dragging down an iPod, but they still carry that buttery beat-matching to glue it all together into a single, cohesive trip. Make no mistake: this is the exact work that put my name on the map long before I got signed and started producing my own tracks. It's the set that gave birth to my worldwide hit "[Teardrop on Roads](teardrop-on-roads)" mashup.

If you're streaming the mix right now, you're listening to version seven.

### The Haunted Release

The very first physical drop was limited to exactly six CDs. Each one was pressed in a different color, styled to look like a tiny vinyl record. They've since gone down in ATX urban legends as the "haunted" release. Some of the discs would randomly skip forward, others would violently rewind, some flat-out refused to play specific tracks, and a few just locked into repeating the exact same song endlessly. All six people who received a copy reported the exact same poltergeist behavior, and every single one of them earned that disc: Tristan Skybreak, Gaea Phoenix, DJ Ezra B Rich, AychEff Zero, Hekate Law, and Keagan Macab.

### Building the Beast

There's a reason CD2, _Tears of Ra_, actually hit the streets before this one in the series. It wasn't about grandstanding or flexing -- it was pure technical survival. I already knew about 60% of what I wanted on _Blood of the Moon_, but I hadn't spent enough time in the trenches with trip-hop, breakbeat, and downtempo to really understand how to stitch those specific dots together. And to be brutally honest? The tracks themselves straight-up refused to play nice with each other, save for a few rare exceptions.

### The Guitar Center Hustle

So, I had to brute-force these tracks together while out on the road hitchhiking. I'd crash local Guitar Centers just to "test out the decks," secretly recording bite-sized mini-mixes of the transitions. Then I'd hit up public libraries across state lines and email those raw pieces back to myself. Over time, each chunk started forging its own distinct identity. Even the hardcore fans use the proper titles for these sections now -- like referring to the heavy collision of "Teardrop" and "Roads" by its true name: _"Sorrow's Path."_

### The 24-Hour Vision

Even though I’m carving these up on my own proper hardware these days, I still tend to mix them down into tight, 15-minute bursts before sending them out into the wild. The ultimate endgame? One day, there needs to be a massive, 24-hour archive of these cuts so people can rip them apart, mix them up, and stitch together their own custom favorites.

To quote the legendary poet himself...

### Blood of the Moon V7 Audio Manifest

1.  **DJ Shadow** - _Building Steam with a Grain of Salt_ (v1+)
2.  **Linkin Park** - _Cure for the Itch_ (v5+)
3.  **The Dust Brothers** - _Jack's Smirking Revenge_ (v1+)
4.  **Bjork** - _All Is Full of Love (Funkstorung remix)_ (v6 - v8)\*
5.  **Massive Attack** - _Teardrop_ (v1+)\*\*
6.  **Portishead** - _Roads_ (v1+)\*\*
7.  **Lamb** - _Trans Fatty Acid_ _(Kruder & Dorfmeister Session Mix)_ (v3+)
8.  **Nine Inch Nails** - _A Warm Place_ (v1+)\*\*\*
9.  **David Holmes** - _Gone (Original Mix vs The Kruder & Dorfmeister Session)_ (v3+)
10.  **Lisahall** - _Is This Real?_ (v1+)
11.  **Nelly Furtado** - _Turn Off the Lights (Remixed by DJ Ezra B Rich)_ (v1+)
12.  **DJ Shadow** - _Midnight in a Perfect World_ (v1+)
13.  **Moby** - _The Sky Is Broken (Jaya Prime Recut)_ (v7+)\*\*\*\*
14.  **Malcom McLaren** - _About Her_ (v1+)
15.  **Faithless** - _Code_ (v3+)
16.  **Faithless** - _Evergreen_ (v3+)
17.  **UNKLE** - _Lonely Soul (Original vs In Tune and On Time)_ (v1+)
18.  **Portishead** - _It's a Fire_ (v5+)

\* Painfully replaced "Fall in the Light" by Lori Carson and Graeme Revell ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TiKFHrg-WOw)), which itself was later replaced with "Glass Veil" by Koda ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z1edsyIQePY)) on the modern MP3 mini-mix of "Sorrow's Path."

\*\* Version 7 was the last to include "Teardrop" and "Roads" separately, as after this I always used my "[Teardrop on Roads](teardrop-on-roads)" mashup.

\*\*\* Version 6 was the only version that included my mashup "All the Warmth in this Memory" mixed into the tail end of the original, which was cut from future mixes.

\*\*\*\* Up until Version 7, the original release-cut of the song was used instead.

### Ready to Receive

As with all the Study in Forces series of DJ mixes, I learned a lot from mixing this set... and it wasn't all about the music nor the alchemy. It's amazing how many of these songs I'd heard beforehand, but wasn't ready to hear them, to receive them, to truly appreciate them! For example, I 100% heard "Roads" when I saw the movie _Tank Girl_, but it didn't mark me until my brother Zero introduced me to it. Marf introduced me to DJ Shadow and played it a lot for me, but it took multiple listens until I was like, "Wait, what song is that?" And of course is was Shadow. Then there are others like "Lonely Soul" that clicked immediately when Loki introduced me to it. My sister Gaea didn't just introduce me to "Is This Real?" but also the movie it came from, _Practical Magic_, which didn't click until we were just jamming out to music together. It's a lesson I brought to my live shows. There's a big difference than playing a show where _you_ are the background music and a show where people have come specifically to see _YOU_... to hear _your_ music. I can name every soul and in every moment where each of these songs truly reached me... when I was ready to receive them.

I feel honored to have been the person to bring these songs to others.

And in the hopes that at least one of these reached you. _Really_ reached you.

### The Shape of Air + Water

"Blood of the Moon" has one of the more unique curves, not just in my DJ mixes but almost any of them. It starts out faster-paced on a high note, then descends and becomes slower going into "A Warm Place" at the middle, only slowly growing and pick up pace again towards the very end -- forming an inverted crescent befitting of the moon herself. "[Tears of Ra](#?/other-dj-mixes)" follows the more standard crescendo, rising to a stead plateau, rising again to the next plateau, then repeat until the cool-off period at the end to wind down.  The final album, "Shadows of Twilight", follows a build more similar to a calm lake where the waves are so small that they crest only in long, quiet ripples. Long-time fans have mentioned the lack of quotes, since mixing in quotes from shows and movies to tell an overarching story has definitely become a signature of my style. The _Study in Forces_ series came before that, a study in the sound itself, in the elemental compositions and how they combine.

Because of this inverted crescent, ever since "Blood of the Moon" I've earned the reputation of playing all the sad songs.

### Design Credit

The back cover as seen here is my collaboration _"Memento Mori"_ (aka, "Man in the Moon") with GreatJester.

## Extended Exploration

In emotion and how it tears into you, "[The Passions of Blood, Smoke, & Oil](the-passions)" DJ set is the spiritual successor to "Blood of the Moon". Then I've already mentioned the "[Teardrop on Roads](teardrop-on-roads)" mashup that was born here in this DJ set and has since spread around the world, even being covered by a live symphony. Then my book "[Memoriam Redacta](memoriam-redacta)" fits the spiritual, emotional, and intellectual themes that go along with this set.
